data.name: Bhure
data.gender_notes: Bhure is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Bhure is derived from Sanskrit, which means 'Lord of Cows'. In Hindu mythology, Lord Krishna is often depicted as the protector of cows. The name Bhure is a symbol of compassion, love, and nurturing, representing the divine caretaker. The name Bhure carries the meaning “Lord of Cows” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhure usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of cows and live with faith, good character and purpose.

It represents the reverence and love for these gentle creatures that are believed to bring prosperity, purity, and good fortune.
data.spiritual_significance: In spiritual terms, Bhure is a reflection of Lord Krishna's caring and nurturing qualities. The name is a reminder of the divine being who protects and nurtures his people and creation. It inspires one to be compassionate, selfless, and caring towards all beings, just like Lord Krishna. The name Bhure offers a sense of hope, security, and strength, reminding one of the divine protective power.
